<reason>A establishes a limited but meaningful additional accountability route: cooperation elsewhere can matter even while the host government remains complicit. B raises serious predictability and enforcement concerns, but overstates them into claims of inherent arbitrariness and practical uselessness. Its domestic-crime redundancy argument does not answer the international enforcement gap. A answers both pressure questions concretely and acknowledges limitations, while B’s closing largely repeats a dilemma that A had substantially answered.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A identifies a knowingly rejected, equally effective and affordable alternative as evidence of clearly excessive damage. B recasts this as destruction offering no benefit, overlooking the distinction between the dam’s overall benefits and its unnecessary additional destruction. That weakens B’s central claim that A supplied no provable fact supporting liability.</best_rebuttal>
